source.prompt: best ERP software for small manufacturing business under 50 employees
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
Selecting an ERP for a shop with under 50 employees comes down to balancing **manufacturing depth** against **implementation complexity**. Full enterprise platforms like SAP or NetSuite often overwhelm small teams and carry six-figure implementation costs, whereas simple inventory tools lack proper Material Requirements Planning (MRP) and shop-floor control.

---

**Top ERP Software for Small Manufacturers**

| ERP Platform | Target Use Case / Fit | Key Strengths | Estimated Pricing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MRPeasy** | Light manufacturing, batch assembly, high growth | Quick deployment, native integration with QuickBooks/Xero, clean UI. | ~$49 – $149 / user / month |
| **Cetec ERP** | Job shops, discrete manufacturing, regulated parts | Full web-native ERP (Shop floor, Quality/ISO, Finance) at low cost. | ~$40 / user / month |
| **JobBOSS²** | Custom job shops, make-to-order (MTO) metal/plastics | Excellent job costing, shop floor control, and time tracking. | Custom (~$100 / user / month) |
| **Odoo (Manufacturing)** | Highly custom workflows, modular growth | Massive app ecosystem, flexible BOMs, open-source base. | ~$25 – $40 / user / month |
| **MS Dynamics 365 Business Central** | Maturing businesses needing formal enterprise controls | Deep finance and supply chain, tight Microsoft 365/Excel integration. | ~$70 – $100 / user / month |

---

**Detailed Platform Breakdown**

**1. MRPeasy (Best for Fast Implementation)**
* **Why it fits:** Designed explicitly for small manufacturers (10–50 employees) who want MRP without replacing their existing accounting software.
* **Core Capabilities:** Work orders, BOM management, shop-floor reporting, material planning, and direct sync with QuickBooks or Xero.
* **Trade-off:** Lacks advanced enterprise-grade custom accounting tools natively; relies on third-party accounting integrations for deep financials.

**2. Cetec ERP (Best Value All-in-One)**
* **Why it fits:** A fully integrated web-based ERP that offers manufacturing, inventory, purchasing, shop floor tracking, and full GL accounting out of the box without hidden module fees.
* **Core Capabilities:** Mobile warehouse management, ISO/Quality management tools, shop floor routing, and trace/lot tracking.
* **Trade-off:** The user interface looks dated compared to modern SaaS apps, though functional.

**3. JobBOSS² (Best for Job Shops & Custom Fabricators)**
* **Why it fits:** Built specifically for make-to-order operations and machine shops where job costing accuracy is critical.
* **Core Capabilities:** Real-time job costing, material calculators, barcoded shop floor data collection, and dynamic capacity scheduling.
* **Trade-off:** Less tailored for process, batch, or high-volume repetitive manufacturing.

**4. Odoo Manufacturing (Best for Modular Flexibility)**
* **Why it fits:** Ideal if you want a modular system where you only pay for what you turn on (e.g., MRP, Inventory, CRM, Quality).
* **Core Capabilities:** Work center tracking, Maintenance app integration, PLM (Product Lifecycle Management), and flexible routings.
* **Trade-off:** Out-of-the-box setups often require custom configuration or a certified implementation partner.

---

**Selection Checklist for Under 50 Employees**

1. **Accounting Strategy:** Do you want to keep your existing accounting software (e.g., QuickBooks) or replace it entirely? 
   * *Keep QuickBooks:* Look at **MRPeasy** or **JobBOSS²**.
   * *Replace everything:* Look at **Cetec ERP** or **Odoo**.
2. **Manufacturing Type:** Make-to-Stock (MTS) needs strong batch/inventory controls (**MRPeasy** / **Cetec**); Make-to-Order (MTO) or custom job shops need strict job-costing (**JobBOSS²**).
3. **Implementation Resources:** Avoid platforms requiring long configuration cycles (6+ months) unless you have dedicated in-house IT.
